rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained (representation). The project checks the box only on a return that files Form 2441 (f2441.filing: care expenses or dependent care benefits); the second tests the provider count alone. A filer with neither does not file the form (i2441 p. 1, Purpose of Form, "you may be able to take the credit for child and dependent care expenses" and "you must use Form 2441 to figure the amount, if any, of the benefits you can exclude"), so there is no box to check; on every return that files it both test "more than three care providers" (i2441 p. 2, Line 1, "If you have more than three care providers, check the box above line 1"). No change to the data.

Ruling: scope; project retained. The second enters zero for a married filing separately filer not treated as unmarried; the project refuses Form 2441 on any married filing separately return (s3.mfs, refused on this line and line 26 and in scope.ready; owner decision 5, "Form 2441 refuses MFS"), so the branch never arises and both take the smaller of lines 9c and 10. i2441 p. 2, Married Persons Filing Separately, "Generally, married persons must file a joint return to claim the credit" and "If you don't meet all of the requirements to be treated as unmarried, you can't generally take the credit". No change to the data.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation after correction BUG-0119; the two trees differ only by the per-person field dependent.dc_line2d versus dependent.dc_paid, an unconditional copy, with identical qualifying-person filters. After BUG-0119 the existing f2441.paid_2026 input asks for every other qualified 2025 incurred expense regardless of payment date, including unpaid expenses. Together the per-person amounts and that nonduplicating supplement meet i2441 (2025) p. 5 Line 16. The prior ruling incorrectly treated a question limited to 2026 payments as covering every payment date; that premise was false and is corrected here, not reused as evidence that the old input was sound. The saved payment-year witness records the former $4000 taxable-benefit overstatement.

Ruling: scope; project retained. The second adds a branch for a married filing separately filer not treated as unmarried (the spouse's earned income as an input); the project refuses every married filing separately return (s3.mfs in scope.ready, and on Form 2441 lines 11 and 26; owner decision 5, "Form 2441 refuses MFS"). On a joint return both take the spouse's earned income, otherwise line 18. f2441 p. 2, line 19, "If married filing jointly, enter your spouse's earned income", "If married filing separately, see instructions. • All others, enter the amount from line 18"; i2441 p. 2, Married Persons Filing Separately, "Generally, married persons must file a joint return". No change to the data.

Ruling: scope; f2441 (2025) p. 2 line 19 and i2441 p. 5 distinguish separate-return spouse income from the considered-unmarried exception. The project refuses married filing separately at f2441.line11/s3.line11. Removing only that excluded filing status leaves the same joint spouse-income branch and other-status line18 branch. This is a completed-return scope ruling, not correctness of this line evaluated alone on an excluded MFS return.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; replacing only sum_over field dependent.dc_count with dependent.one makes the two canonical trees exactly equal, including the qualifying-person predicate. Both Count fields are unconditional copies of the same dependent.one parameter. f2441 (2025) p. 1 line 2 box and i2441 p. 3 Line 2 count qualifying persons, not all dependents. No predicate or amount is changed.

Ruling: representation; subtract_floor0(x,0) and larger_of(x,0) both equal max(x,0), with the exact same canonical x=min(line19,min(line17,line18)). f2441 (2025) p. 2 line 20 requires that minimum and the nonpositive floor. The constant zero introduces no additional input or refusal.

Ruling: scope; project retained. The second halves the $5,000 for a married filing separately filer not treated as unmarried; the project refuses every married filing separately return (s3.mfs in scope.ready, and on lines 11 and 26, whose refusal names "lines 19 and 21"; owner decision 5), so the $2,500 case never arises and both enter the smaller of $5,000 and the plan maximum. f2441 p. 2, line 21, "Enter $5,000 ($2,500 if married filing separately and you were required to enter your spouse's earned income on line 19)"; i2441 p. 5, Line 21. No change to the data.

Ruling: project retained (representation). The two agree on every return. Line 24 is the smallest of lines 20, 21 and 22, so with "No" on line 22 (line 22 zero) line 24 is zero and the project's subtraction gives the smaller of lines 20 and 21, which is the second's first branch; otherwise both subtract line 24 (f2441 p. 2, line 25, "If you checked “No” on line 22, enter the smaller of line 20 or line 21. Otherwise, subtract line 24 from the smaller of line 20 or line 21"). Line 22 is in any case zero here, the Yes cases being refused (sc.special, scope.schedule1, scope.other_income). No change to the data.

The project asks column (d) per person including expenses paid with dependent care benefits (dependent.dc_paid) and figures line 30 as their total less line 28, not less than zero; the second reads column (d) as already net of the benefits. The form says "Don’t include in column (d) any benefits shown on line 28 above. Then, add the amounts in column (d) and enter the total here" (f2441 p. 2, line 30) and gives no rule for dividing line 28 among the persons; that is the ambiguity the register records, with the project's reading chosen. No change to the data.

Ruling: scope; f2441 (2025) p. 1 line 5 uses spouse earned income for a joint return and line 4 otherwise. Pub. 503 (2025) p. 11 Surviving spouse permits a choice for a deceased spouse. That joint/deceased case is expressly refused by f2441.spouse_died_gate at project line 5. On an admitted joint return the added not-deceased guard is true and the two alternatives reduce to the project; on admitted nonjoint returns both choose line 4. Retain the narrower supported computation; no claim is made for the excluded surviving-spouse choice or partial inputs.

Ruling: scope; project retained. The second applies Pub. 503's surviving-spouse choice and enters line 4 when the spouse died in 2025; the project refuses that case (f2441.spouse_died_gate, joint return with f2441.spouse_died Yes, refused on lines 5 and 19; owner decision 5, "a spouse who died in 2025"), so on every return it computes the spouse died in 2025 is No and both take the spouse's earned income. p503 p. 11, Surviving spouse, "you may, but aren't required to, take into account the earned income of your spouse who died during the year"; i2441 p. 4, "If your spouse died in 2025, see Pub. 503". No change to the data.
